Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

RECOMMENDED SHAPES, SIZES AND MASS OF 

COPPER AND COPPER ALLOY INGOTS 

FOR REMELTING PURPOSES 



1. Scope — This standard specifies shapes, sizes and mass of copper and copper alloy ingcts used 
for rennelting purposes. 

2. Shapes, Sizes and Mass 

2.1 Six types of shapes, sizes and mass of ingots generally used in industry are shown in Fig. 1 to 9. 
The dimensions and mass indicated are nominal ( tor reference and guidance only).

FIG. 1 TO 9 SHAPES, SIZES AND MASS OF COPPER AND COPPER ALLOYS INGOTS 

2.2 Selection of a particular shape, size and mass is to be decided according to the design and size of 
the melting furnace. 

2.3 Apart from the types given in this standard, any other shape, size and mass may be manufactured 
as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

3, Marking— All ingots shall have such markings as may have been specified in the appropriate 
Indian Standard. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Ingots 3re used for remelting purposes in the manufacture of alloys for castings or for alloy ingots 
for use in foundries. In order to unify the shapes and sizes of ingots to which reference fias boeri 
made in the various relevant Indian Standards and also to assist the purchaser and the manufacturer in 
their day-to-day transactions, need for such a standard was felt. The shapes and sizes given m this 
standard have been based on their long use and practice in tiie copper industry.
